Matched RecHarness Amazon task: four datasets Movies_and_TV,
Industrial_and_Scientific, Electronics, CDs_and_Vinyl, macro-average validation
HR@10. Start from RecHarness sasrec_perdataset. Preprocessing seed=0 and training
seed=42, exactly as run2.sh. The host executes your train.py and then independently
evaluates working/predict.py using the pinned RecHarness benchmark (200 validation
users/category, 99 unique negative candidates, evaluation seed=42). Test labels and
test metrics are unavailable during search. Retain all four categories and dataset
routing. DATA_DIR must remain os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR']; write artifacts beneath
your trial directory, as the baseline does. Training may change model architecture,
loss, optimizer, sampling and hyperparameters, as in RecHarness. Do not alter input
splits, invent metrics, read hidden test files, fetch extra datasets/pretrained weights,
or change the host evaluator. Changes to inference must also update the predictor
writer so working/predict.py loads the trained architecture. Keep execution single-GPU;
the host provides four concurrent trial slots and 64 CPU cores. No shell actions,
filesystem inspection, or training tools are needed in the LLM call: return code.
All training, diagnostics, debugging and failed trials consume the method's shared
43,200 GPU-second search budget. LLM time and final held-out inference are recorded
separately, matching run2.sh's separate final-evaluation step.
The original RecHarness tools layer sets SASREC_EPOCHS=200 (overriding the template's
standalone default of 300); this same environment default applies here.

METHOD: self_evolverec

Diagnostic task adapter: diagnosis_tools.py must retain class DiagnosisProbe(view, device)
and method run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), returning metrics and metric_definitions.
It must also retain callable diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis), returning
the diagnostic interpretation prompt using measured metrics and their definitions.
view.model is the actual trained nn.Module. view.item_emb, log2feats(sequence),
predict_score(features, items), user_train, meta_data, review_data implement the
initial SASRec compatibility contract. Adapt probes when changing the architecture.
train_loader yields (None, sequence, positive, negative), tensors of shape B x L.
Only public interaction histories, item titles, descriptions and timestamps are available.
Review ratings/text, item ratings/categories/prices/stores are NOT available in this
shared RecHarness task. Never invent them. Simulator diversity/conformity traits are
explicitly unobserved. Twenty real training users (five/category) receive full-catalog
unseen-item recommendations, as the native simulator requires. Selection uses the
common macro validation HR@10, replacing the native HR@5/NDCG@5 combined score.

NATIVE ROLE: Reflection Agent

You are an expert research assistant. You will receive a research report (in Markdown) and a newly proposed idea for that report's research problem. Your job is to identify any gaps or issues—such as missing details, logical flaws, or questionable evaluations of novelty, impact, or implementation difficulty.  

- If the report and idea contain all necessary information, do not generate any follow-up questions.  
- If you detect a knowledge gap or something that needs deeper exploration, generate one or more self-contained follow-up queries. Each query must include enough context so that a web search could answer it, For each query, give a short note explaining why you use the query and what you hope it will reveal.
- Focus on technical details, implementation specifics, and any emerging methods or references that were overlooked.  
- Use clear, direct language and avoid unnecessary jargon.

 ## Search results
Evidence supports testing more negatives before aggressive hard mining. [gSASRec (IJCAI 2024)](https://www.ijcai.org/proceedings/2024/0939.pdf) combines multiple uniform negatives with calibrated gBCE to reduce sampled-BCE overconfidence; authors recommend 128–256 negatives and calibration t=0.75, with higher compute costs. [RecSys 2025’s sampled-softmax implementation](https://github.com/NonameUntitled/logq/) provides uniform, in-batch and mixed sampling, plus revised logQ correction—useful alternatives when comparing candidate competition without changing the encoder. These results do not establish gains on the four target Amazon categories.

Hardest-only mining risks false negatives and unstable early training. [R2NS (WWW 2026)](https://renzhaochun.github.io/assets/pdf/WWW_2026_Camera_Ready.pdf) uses uniform warm-up, efficient global candidate recall and progressively harder stochastic selection. It explains why sampling among top-ranked candidates can reduce false-negative risk relative to always choosing the maximum. [CATS (2026)](https://iris.uniroma1.it/handle/11573/1775773) instead uses item clusters and adaptive sampling to reduce repeated selection of likely false negatives near the positive item.

Suggested controlled ablation: retain single-negative BCE as baseline; compare sampled softmax with 16/64/128 uniform negatives and gBCE with 128 negatives; then test a modest random/hard mixture after warm-up. Exclude padding, the target and observed training positives; sample stochastically among hard candidates. These controls cannot identify every unobserved positive. Electronics’ reported 14.95% outranking rate motivates investigation but does not prove mining will help. Select exclusively by unchanged four-category macro validation HR@10, tracking GPU time and category-level regressions.

---

Recent work challenges a single sequence vector through separate temporal and interest pathways. [HeteroTempRec (2026)](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ins.2025.122703) combines convolutional local-pattern extraction, transformer global dependencies, and personalized temporal fusion; sparse block attention limits computation. [MGUI (2026)](https://doi.org/10.1109/TCSS.2026.3675684) combines time-interval-aware gating of recent items, capsule-guided group interests, and cross-sequence transition graphs, with a user-specific mixture of experts. Both provide architectural precedents for adaptively weighting immediate context against broader preferences.

Sparsity and noisy histories motivate complementary approaches. [LS4SRec (2025)](https://doi.org/10.1145/3723173) separates long- and short-term encoders and adds collaborative information from a global interaction-transition graph. [D2MFRec (published December 2025)](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41598-025-31190-z) gates single-interest and multiple-interest representations, then applies denoising and contrastive learning. Its reported datasets are MovieLens and Yelp, so transfer to sparse Amazon histories remains unproven.

Practical inference for this benchmark: retain SASRec as one expert; add a recent-window expert and attention-pooled historical preference expert. Gate their scores using observed history length, elapsed-time features, and disagreement between recent and historical representations. Use only timestamps available at prediction time; mask padding and preserve causal training. Start with two or three experts to constrain computation and overfitting, then ablate time features and gating under macro validation HR@10. These are proposed adaptations, not established benchmark gains. Interaction recency supplies evidence about predictive relevance; it does not establish ownership, satisfaction, or exhausted demand.

---

Recent work supports learning directional continuation signals separately from item similarity. [DTR4Rec (2024 online/2025 volume)](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s10489-024-05875-3) counts long-window directed transitions and short-window co-occurrences, then learns their fusion with sequence predictions; its experiments include Amazon Beauty and Sports. [GLSRec (2026)](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0169023X26000534) combines lightweight graph propagation, global transition calibration of item embeddings, and local MLP sequence mixers. [Revisiting Graph Projections (2025)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.09209) offers a simpler complementary-product approach using a directed weighted projection of historical user–item interactions. These motivate inexpensive transition-based additions before a larger GNN.

Complementarity and substitution require care: [TransGAT (ICDM 2024)](https://ieeexplore.ieee.org/document/10884336/) explicitly encodes behavioral direction and jointly models complement/substitute graphs, but observed next-item transitions alone do not establish either relationship. For this benchmark, a proposed adaptation—not a verified result—is a separate sparse directed graph per category, built exclusively from training histories, with distinct source/target embeddings or incoming/outgoing aggregation and a learned residual score alongside SASRec. Optional title/description features could use locally fitted TF-IDF projections or randomly initialized pooled token embeddings trained jointly. ## Starting Research Idea
SASRec predicts the next item by applying causal self-attention to interaction histories. Learned item and positional embeddings pass through attention and feed-forward blocks with residual connections, normalization and dropout. Final sequence features score candidates through shared item embeddings. [Paper](https://arxiv.org/html/1808.09781)
